overview.heading: Agricultural study near Hosur
paragraphs: Adhiyamaan College of Agriculture and Research was established by AERI Trust in 2016. The college describes a 122.5-acre setting at Athimugam, around 22 kilometres from Hosur. Its TNAU affiliation provides the academic framework for the undergraduate agriculture programme.

The degree brings together crop improvement, plant protection, agricultural engineering, economics and extension. overview.heading: Agriculture education on the Chennai–Trichy corridor
paragraphs: JSA College of Agriculture and Technology is based around Ma. Podaiyur and Avatti, near Tholudhur in Cuddalore district. hero.title: The Indian Agriculture College
hero.summary: TIAC is an agriculture college in Radhapuram, Tirunelveli district, affiliated to TNAU. Established in 2016 under Joshua Educational and Charitable Trust, it focuses on agricultural education and the farming needs of southern Tamil Nadu. Its verified ICAR entry covers the agriculture undergraduate degree.

overview.heading: Agricultural education in southern Tamil Nadu
paragraphs: The Indian Agriculture College is located on the Kavalkinaru–Radhapuram Road in Tirunelveli district. Established in 2016 under Joshua Educational and Charitable Trust, it focuses on agricultural education and the farming needs of southern Tamil Nadu.

Its four-year degree is organised over eight semesters. The course page covers agricultural science alongside surveying, soils, water management and allied subjects. The college also publishes campus material grouped around laboratories, agricultural fields, farms and industrial visits. Applicants can use those resources to identify which practical areas interest them and request the current timetable for field and laboratory learning.

overview.heading: A Vellore district college focused on agriculture
paragraphs: Palar Agricultural College was established in 2017 under RS Educational and Charitable Trust. It is located at Kothamarikuppam Village, Mailpatti Post, in Vellore district and offers a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture under TNAU affiliation.

Its academic divisions cover crop science and associated subjects, with agricultural teaching units and student-support cells listed across the campus website. overview.heading: Agriculture and rural development at Valikandapuram
paragraphs: Thanthai Roever Institute of Agriculture and Rural Development belongs to the Roever educational group and is run by St. John Sangam Trust. Its history records agriculture diploma teaching from 1994 and horticulture diploma teaching from 2001, with degree education developed later.

hero.title: Khalsa College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
hero.summary: KCVAS is a veterinary college in Amritsar affiliated to GADVASU. Its animal-health teaching is supported by a Veterinary Clinical Complex at Mahal with small- and large-animal services. The degree profiled here is B.V.Sc. & A.H., with no agriculture B.Sc. scope inferred.

overview.heading: Veterinary learning with clinical exposure at Mahal
paragraphs: Khalsa College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences was established by Khalsa College Charitable Society. The college dates its formation to 2009 and GADVASU affiliation to 2010. It focuses on veterinary health, animal production and management, making it a distinct option from an undergraduate crop-science college.

Its Veterinary Clinical Complex is at village Mahal on Ram Tirath Road, separate from the main campus. The department describes services for small and large animals, diagnostic imaging, surgery and clinical laboratory work. For applicants, that clinical setting is central to evaluating the programme: ask how clinical rotations, case exposure and internship supervision are organised for the intended cohort.

programmes.name: B.V.Sc. & A.H.
programmes.summary: B.V.Sc. & A.H. is a 5½-year veterinary programme in the GADVASU admission rules. KCVAS combines veterinary study with clinical and animal-management teaching; professional-registration conditions should be checked with the relevant authorities.
programmes.eligibility: GADVASU’s NEET-UG-2026 rules require 10+2 or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English and 50% aggregate excluding optional subjects (47.5% for SC/ST, BC and DP categories), plus the relevant NEET cutoff. Category, domicile and quota conditions also apply.
programmes.admission_route: GADVASU’s 2026 rules refer to NEET-UG-2026 eligibility and counselling. Different quota and domicile conditions must be checked in the current official notice.

hero.title: Khalsa College, Amritsar
hero.summary: Khalsa College is an autonomous affiliated college in Amritsar, founded in 1892. Its agriculture department publishes crop-science teaching, rural work experience and experiential-learning activities. This profile concerns the college’s agriculture degree, distinct from the separately affiliated Khalsa veterinary college.

overview.heading: Agriculture within a historic Amritsar college
paragraphs: Khalsa College was established in 1892 and is affiliated to Guru Nanak Dev University. Its agriculture department has a long academic history: the official department account records degree affiliation to Panjab University in 1931 and then GNDU in 1971, with postgraduate teaching developed in 1967.

The department describes dedicated agricultural teaching blocks and laboratories covering agronomy, crop protection, soil science, horticulture and agricultural economics. Its activity archive includes rural work experience, commercial beekeeping, mushroom cultivation and paddy-residue-management programmes. These dated examples help applicants understand the department’s practical orientation while leaving the current cohort’s exact activity calendar for direct confirmation.

hero.title: AKS University
hero.summary: AKS University in Satna offers agriculture through its Faculty of Agriculture Science and Technology. Its published curriculum spans crop science, horticulture and agricultural engineering, while the Department of Agronomy connects teaching with crop research and extension work.

overview.heading: Crop science within a wider agricultural faculty
paragraphs: The undergraduate agriculture course at AKS sits within a faculty that also publishes curricula for agricultural engineering, food technology and several postgraduate agricultural subjects. This allows applicants to distinguish a broad first degree from later specialist study rather than treating every agriculture-related course as the same qualification.

The agronomy department dates its establishment to 2014. Its published teaching and research interests include crop production, soil management and weed control. The department also describes farmer training and field demonstrations, giving a concrete extension context to academic work. Applicants can progress from the broad undergraduate degree to specialist agronomy study, subject to the published qualification and practical-work requirements.

The school’s stated priorities include crop management, postharvest value addition and knowledge transfer to farming communities in southern Rajasthan.

overview.heading: Agricultural education with a southern Rajasthan focus
paragraphs: The School of Agricultural Sciences is based at the university’s Dabok campus, rather than simply sharing the central administrative address in Udaipur. Its published teaching objectives address crop and pest management, preventing postharvest losses and taking agricultural knowledge to farming communities. These priorities provide useful context for applicants interested in extension as well as production science.

The official school page lists B.Sc. Agriculture, several M.Sc. Agriculture and Horticulture specialisations, an agribusiness MBA and doctoral study. These are distinct awards with different academic entry points. The published postgraduate list includes crop production, plant health, agricultural economics, extension and livestock management, together with fruit, vegetable and ornamental horticulture.

hero.title: Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences
hero.summary: Karunya’s School of Agricultural Sciences in Coimbatore describes a substantial instructional farm, protected cultivation structures and subject divisions. It offers undergraduate agriculture and specialist postgraduate courses, with field experiments and entrepreneurship modules forming part of its published educational account.

overview.heading: Field-based agricultural study in Coimbatore
paragraphs: Karunya dates its School of Agricultural Sciences to 2017. The current school page describes eleven academic divisions, covering crop, soil, plant-health, engineering and allied subjects. Its farm and laboratory setting supports a programme account that extends beyond lecture teaching to crop experiments, protected cultivation and agricultural enterprise learning.

Official sources list a four-year B.Sc. Agriculture together with postgraduate agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, and fruit science. These subject options allow students to distinguish crop production, crop improvement and horticultural study. Entry wording differs between the academics page and the brochure located during research, so applicants need the definitive course notice before selecting a school-subject or postgraduate route.

hero.title: Rabindranath Tagore University
hero.summary: Rabindranath Tagore University’s Faculty of Agriculture began undergraduate teaching in 2015-16 in Raisen district near Bhopal. Its four-year agriculture programme links crop and soil science with rural work, agricultural enterprises and a research farm supported by irrigation and machinery.

overview.heading: Agriculture teaching with a rural development context
paragraphs: RNTU’s agriculture faculty describes its original purpose as expanding agricultural education in underserved parts of Raisen district. The degree began in 2015-16. The current course account covers agronomy, horticulture, soil science, plant health, breeding, economics and extension, bringing production science and the social setting of farming into the same undergraduate route.

The published programme structure includes village surveys, soil sampling, plant-protection interventions and agro-industrial attachment. It also lists enterprise learning options such as beekeeping, mushroom cultivation and seed production. These are curriculum descriptions; applicants should ask which modules will actually run for their cohort and how the practical timetable is organised.

overview.heading: An affiliated agriculture college at Kapasan

overview.heading: Agriculture, agronomy and entomology at Mullana
paragraphs: The university’s agriculture pathway includes a four-year B.Sc. and two-year master’s degrees in agronomy and entomology. The 2026-27 information booklet specifies qualifying subjects and marks for each route.

The faculty’s self-study report identifies a teaching museum of agricultural tools, seeds and models, plus postgraduate laboratories and research plots. A May 2026 university account also records agricultural expert discussions and describes experimental farms. These sources support a practical learning context; they do not establish a typical graduate salary or a guaranteed appointment.

hero.title: The Neotia University
hero.summary: At Sarisa in West Bengal, The Neotia University brings crop science, laboratory work and rural learning together through its School of Agriculture and Allied Sciences. Its four-year agriculture degree includes village attachment and agro-industrial experience, with teaching extending across soils, crops, plant protection, horticulture and farm economics.

overview.heading: Agriculture study near Diamond Harbour
paragraphs: TNU’s agriculture course connects crop science with work in farming environments. Its published curriculum includes soil science, horticulture, plant protection, genetics and agricultural economics. The degree page describes four years of study, with rural agricultural experience and an agro-industrial attachment in the final stage.

The school’s older official brochure describes teaching farms, laboratories and small production units, including mushroom and apiculture activity. Such settings connect scientific observation with day-to-day production decisions. The 2026–27 fee schedule identifies the agriculture bachelor’s degree alongside agribusiness, diploma and postgraduate routes, giving applicants distinct study options to compare.

overview.heading: Two allied schools within one Odisha university

Its school page identifies agronomy, crop improvement, horticulture, soil science and extension as teaching and research areas. The School of Fisheries provides another applied pathway at Paralakhemundi. Its regulations describe aquaculture, fish processing, aquatic health and resource management, supported by training ponds, a hatchery and specialist production activity. Agriculture and fisheries therefore offer different practical settings within the university, and applicants can compare crop-based, engineering, agribusiness and aquatic-science routes according to their interests.

hero.summary: LPU’s School of Agriculture in Phagwara brings crop, livestock and post-harvest learning into one academic setting. Farms, a dairy unit, protected cultivation and subject laboratories support its broad bachelor’s programme, while master’s routes offer specialisation in production, crop improvement, plant protection, soils and horticultural subjects.

overview.heading: Agriculture foundations and specialist postgraduate study
paragraphs: LPU’s agriculture school brings crop, livestock and post-harvest learning into one academic setting. Its facilities page identifies an animal husbandry and dairy unit, agricultural farms and subject laboratories. The breadth matters when comparing a general agriculture degree with a focused postgraduate specialisation.

The bachelor’s degree offers a broad entry to agriculture, while the school’s master’s subjects allow a closer focus on agronomy, genetics, plant protection, soils or horticulture. These choices share an agricultural setting but serve different stages of study. The official CUET 2026 mapping supplies a dated bachelor’s eligibility reference, and the admissions office can clarify how that route fits the intended intake.

hero.summary: Kalasalingam’s agriculture school at Krishnankoil connects crop science with a teaching farm, irrigation equipment and subject laboratories. overview.heading: Agriculture teaching in the Krishnankoil setting
paragraphs: KARE’s published agriculture curriculum links crop production and improvement with natural resources, agricultural economics and extension. The 2022 syllabus provides a detailed academic reference for prospective students who want to examine course content beyond a programme title.

The Kalasalingam Anandammal Farm gives the school a practical setting for crop work. The course page identifies fertigation equipment and implements including a tractor, cultivator, disc plough and rotary tiller, alongside nine subject laboratories. Together, these facilities connect the curriculum’s biological and resource-management subjects with cultivation and machinery. KARE’s institutional history begins with an engineering college in 1984 and records university status from 2006.

hero.title: Sri Kinjarapu Yerran Naidu College of Agricultural Sciences
hero.summary: Sri Kinjarapu Yerran Naidu College of Agricultural Sciences offers undergraduate agriculture at Etcherla in Srikakulam district. Established in 2016, the privately managed college is affiliated to Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University, whose 2026–27 Category A counselling framework includes the college among participating agriculture institutions.

overview.heading: An affiliated agriculture college at Etcherla
paragraphs: ANGRAU distinguishes SKYCAS from its constituent government colleges by listing it among affiliated agriculture colleges. The directory places it at Etcherla and gives 2016 as its establishment year. The college therefore needs to be assessed as an affiliated institution with its own teaching setting, while the university provides the academic and admission framework described in official notices.

For the 2026–27 session, the college is included in ANGRAU’s brochure for participating affiliated institutions. Category A admission uses AP EAPCET 2026 ranks, making the university’s counselling instructions central to the application process. Students comparing an affiliated college with an ANGRAU constituent college should check the named institution and admission category carefully, because the college identity and the university’s academic framework play different roles.

hero.title: Shri Shivaji Agriculture College, Amravati
hero.summary: Shri Shivaji Agriculture College in Amravati is run by Shri Shivaji Education Society and affiliated to Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola. Its academic departments cover crop production, plant protection, resources and allied subjects. The college combines a longstanding regional identity with an agriculture bachelor’s programme.

overview.heading: Agricultural education rooted in Amravati
paragraphs: The college traces its founding to Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh and is managed by Shri Shivaji Education Society. Its official history records earlier affiliation to Nagpur University, followed by agricultural-university affiliation. It identifies Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola, as the present affiliating university.

Its departmental structure includes agronomy and meteorology, agricultural botany, chemistry, engineering, horticulture and plant pathology. That spread places crop production alongside weather, soils, equipment and crop health in the college’s teaching setting. The official facilities page describes library and internet resources, and the homepage also mentions postgraduate work in agricultural economics and extension. The college’s affiliation gives applicants a clear university framework for comparing its undergraduate agriculture route.

hero.title: Tilak Dhari P.G. College, Jaunpur
hero.summary: Agriculture at T.D. College sits within a long-established Jaunpur college, with undergraduate study and postgraduate routes across crop production, economics, extension and plant protection. Its agriculture departments give students a subject-based academic setting within a college affiliated to Veer Bahadur Singh Purvanchal University.

overview.heading: Agriculture departments within a historic Jaunpur college
paragraphs: T.D. College traces its origins to a school founded by Sri Tilak Dhari Singh in 1914; its own history dates degree-college status to July 1947. Located in Husainabad, Jaunpur, it is a privately managed grant-in-aid college affiliated to Veer Bahadur Singh Purvanchal University. The founding year therefore describes the institution’s origins rather than the start of degree-level agriculture.

The agriculture faculty spans agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, agricultural economics, engineering, entomology, extension, horticulture, plant pathology, animal husbandry and soil science. The undergraduate agriculture degree is complemented by six postgraduate specialisms in the ICAR register. Applicants interested in a particular specialism can compare the departmental faculty list and the current entrance bulletin before choosing a route.

faqs.question: Is T.D. College a university?
faqs.answer: It is an affiliated college. The audited entry identifies Veer Bahadur Singh Purvanchal University as its parent university; the college remains the teaching institution.

faqs.question: Does 1914 mark the start of degree courses?
faqs.answer: No. The history traces the institution to a school established in 1914 and dates degree-college status to July 1947.

faqs.question: Which agriculture master’s subjects are listed by ICAR?
faqs.answer: The audited scope covers agronomy, agricultural economics, agricultural extension education, entomology, genetics and plant breeding, and plant pathology. Each printed master’s intake is 20. These are accreditation entries rather than live vacancy figures.

faqs.question: Why do agriculture degree names and seats differ between pages?
faqs.answer: The ICAR row prints B.S. (Hons). Agriculture with intake 240, while the older department page calls it B.Sc. (Ag) Hons. and shows 220. The current entrance bulletin should settle the name and seats offered for an admission session.

faqs.question: Where can applicants contact the college?
faqs.answer: The official contact page gives Husainabad, Jaunpur 222002, phone +91 7068319555 and principaltdc1914@gmail.com.

faqs.question: Are current agriculture fees published in this draft?
faqs.answer: No. The official fee page displayed an image without a readable year-specific agriculture table. A dated fee schedule is needed to separate tuition, examination and other charges.
